About

Strategy first.
Story always.


I grew up reading blogs. Everything I know about communication, persuasion, and what makes people actually pay attention came from that. That's not a coincidence. It's the foundation of how I think about content strategy: what does this reader need, and how do we make sure they find it?

I'm Nidhi Agarwal, a content strategist with a background in Digital marketing and English Literature. I combine data and editorial thinking to produce content that resonates with the audience, and at the same time, helps brands become more visible. I have over 3 years of experience in content. I know why it underperforms. I know how to fix it.

At Affable.ai, my last job, I worked as an SEO content writer who helped build and execute content strategies that almost doubled our blog readership. Our strategy was not to publish more, but to be more deliberate about what we published, who we wrote it for, and how we made it searchable. We made content systematic, measurable, and built to last.

How I work

What a content strategist
actually does.

Not just writing. Building the thinking behind what gets published, why, and how success gets measured.

01
Audience & Market Research
Understanding who the reader is, what they're searching for, and what gap in the market the content can fill. Every strategy starts here — before a single word is written.
02
SEO Architecture & Planning
Keyword clustering, content mapping, topic authority building, and editorial calendars designed to create compounding organic traffic — not one-off articles.
03
Performance & Optimisation
Monthly reporting, content audits, and data-backed decisions. Knowing which pieces to update, consolidate, or cut. Strategy doesn't stop at publish.

SEO Content Strategy · Affable.ai · Feb 2022
KOL Influencer Marketing: Why Is It Important For Brands?

The objective was to own the "KOL influencer marketing" keyword cluster — a high-intent search query from brand marketers. The content was structured deliberately to earn a featured snippet: answering the core question within the first 60 words, with a clear hierarchy Google could extract. Result: position #1, featured snippet secured.

Strategic decision: Featured snippets require deliberate content architecture — not just good writing. This was built to win that position from the first draft.

SEO Content Strategy · Affable.ai · March 2022
Top 50 D2C Brands In The US You Should Know About

The challenge: compete against 1.6 million results with a domain that had far less authority than competitors. The strategy was keyword clustering — instead of one keyword, the content was built to rank for an entire cluster simultaneously. It reached positions 2–5 across multiple D2C searches, delivering consistent traffic from brand marketers and e-commerce teams.

Strategic decision: One comprehensive piece targeting a keyword cluster multiplies traffic potential without multiplying content volume. This is how you do more with less.

A Detailed Guide To Health & Wellness Influencer Marketing

Strategy Sample

Thinking applied to
a real brand.

A full content strategy analysis of Plum Goodness — covering their blog, Instagram, SEO gaps, audience blindspots, and three specific strategic recommendations.

Content Strategy Analysis · D2C Skincare
Plum Goodness — Where the Strategy Is Working, and Where It Isn't
Blog · Instagram · SEO · Audience Research · Recommendations

"Plum has the brand presence and product range to lead the Indian skincare content space. What's holding them back is a content strategy that reacts to trends instead of building a system — and content that talks about the brand instead of the audience."

Key Finding 1
The blog targets trending and seasonal keywords but misses high-volume, evergreen searches that beginners type — "how to start a skincare routine," "how to know your skin type." These are the highest-intent readers Plum isn't capturing.
Key Finding 2
The male skincare audience is almost completely unaddressed. Plum has the Phy sub-brand — the product infrastructure is there. The content strategy hasn't caught up with the opportunity.
Key Finding 3
Blog and Instagram are completely disconnected operations — one SEO-driven, one campaign-driven. Neither feeds the other. A connected content pipeline would significantly increase the value of both.
Key Finding 4
Instagram is getting millions of views but engagement is low — which means the content is stopping the scroll but not creating real connection. The content is brand-centric when it should be audience-centric.
